title: Endpoint-fixed mixed-inner-horn refinement
statement: Use simplicial sets and quasicategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], categorical equivalences and Joyal fibrations of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and inner fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $r:Y\to\Delta^1$ be a map with $Y$ a small quasicategory, and let $a:X\to Y$ be a categorical equivalence with $X$ small. Suppose each endpoint map $X_e\to Y_e$ is an isomorphism, with the endpoint fibres identified. If $r$ is an inner fibration, there is a factorization over $\Delta^1$, $X\xrightarrow{j}M\xrightarrow{k}Y$, in which the endpoint fibres of $M$ are exactly those of $X$ and both endpoint maps are identities, $j$ is degreewise injective and a categorical equivalence, and $k$ is a trivial Joyal fibration. The map $j$ is obtained as a countable continuous composite of pushouts of small coproducts of inner horns over simplices of $Y$ having nonconstant $\Delta^1$-coordinate; hence no endpoint simplex is added. The assertion includes empty endpoint fibres and does not require $a$ to be injective.

source.place: HTT Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Corollary 2.2.5.4, restricted mixed-inner-horn small-object refinement (returned item step 4). Agent formulation of the explicit construction retained from the returned item. WANTED: archival source in literature/. No Stacks tag states this construction.

proof.text:
Put $X^{(0)}=X$ and $a_0=a$. Given the small simplicial map $a_t:X^{(t)}\to Y$, take the set $I_t$ of all tuples $(n,i,u,v)$ with $n\geq2$, $0<i<n$, $u:\Lambda_i^n\to X^{(t)}$, $v:\Delta^n\to Y$, $a_tu=v|_{\Lambda_i^n}$, and $rv:\Delta^n\to\Delta^1$ nonconstant. It is a small set: there are countably many $(n,i)$ and sets of maps between small simplicial sets. Define
$$X^{(t+1)}=X^{(t)}\amalg_{\coprod_{I_t}\Lambda_i^n}\coprod_{I_t}\Delta^n.$$
The maps $a_t$ and the listed $v$ induce $a_{t+1}$. Form $M=\operatorname{colim}_{t<\omega}X^{(t)}$, with $j:X\to M$ and $k:M\to Y$ induced by these compatible maps. The sectionwise-colimit lemma applies to set-valued presheaves on the small simplex category, so these pushouts and this colimit are computed degreewise. Explicitly a set pushout is the disjoint union modulo the attaching relations, and a sequential colimit is the disjoint union modulo the transition relations; both are small sets. Simplicial operators descend through the relations. Thus all stages and $M$ are small simplicial sets, $kj=a$, and all maps are over $\Delta^1$.

proof.text:
Each coproduct of horn inclusions is degreewise injective. In a pushout $A\amalg_H B$ with $H\hookrightarrow B$ injective, the old elements of $A$ remain distinct: the only identifications replace an element of $H\subseteq B$ by its specified image in $A$. Equivalently its underlying set can be chosen as $A\amalg(B\setminus H)$. Consequently every transition $X^{(t)}\to X^{(t+1)}$ and $j$ is degreewise injective.
For a cell let $\alpha:[n]\to[1]$ be its nonconstant interval coordinate. Both sets of endpoint vertices are nonempty. Any simplex of $\Delta^n$ with constant coordinate has image in a pure endpoint face $S\subsetneq[n]$. There exists $q\notin S$ with $q\ne i$: otherwise $S=[n]\setminus\{i\}$ and monotonicity of $\alpha$ would make a nonconstant sequence constant after deletion of an interior index, which is impossible since indices $0,n$ remain. Hence this simplex lies in the face omitting $q$, and therefore in $\Lambda_i^n$. No complement $\Delta^n_m\setminus(\Lambda_i^n)_m$ contains an endpoint simplex. Choose the pushouts in the displayed set form. Inductively both endpoint subobjects remain literally $X_e$, with unchanged operators and maps. Their union at $\omega$ is again $X_e$, so $j_e$ and $k_e$ are identities under the stipulated identification $X_e=Y_e$.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph beginning “For K”, through the retained operadic mapping-cylinder refinement: degreewise injectivity and fixed endpoint fibres

proof.text:
Consider an inner-horn lifting problem for $k$ with upper map $u:\Lambda_i^n\to M$ and lower simplex $v:\Delta^n\to Y$. If $rv$ is nonconstant, $u$ factors through some finite stage. Indeed, the horn is the union of its finitely many faces $\Delta^{[n]\setminus\{q\}}$, $q\ne i$. The restriction to each such face is determined by the image of its top simplex: all its other simplices are obtained by precomposition. Choose one stage containing these finitely many images. On the intersections the face maps agree at that stage, since its inclusion into $M$ is degreewise injective; they therefore glue to a map $\Lambda_i^n\to X^{(t)}$. The same equality with $v$ holds after $a_t$, since $k$ restricts to $a_t$. The tuple occurs in $I_t$, so its adjoined simplex at stage $t+1$ fills the original square.
If $rv$ is constant at $e$, the entire upper horn lies in $M_e=X_e$ and the lower simplex lies in $Y_e$. Since $k_e$ is the identity, $v$, regarded as a simplex of $M_e$, is the required filler. These two cases prove that $k$ is an inner fibration, with no assumption that $a$ is injective.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph beginning “For K”, through the retained operadic mapping-cylinder refinement: every relative inner horn receives a filler

proof.text: The simplicial set $M$ is a quasicategory. Given any inner horn in $M$, first fill its image in $Y$, which is a quasicategory by hypothesis, and then lift that chosen filler through the inner fibration $k$ of step 3. This gives a simplex of $M$ extending the original horn. This verification does not presume that the initial $X$ is a quasicategory.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph beginning “For K”, through the retained operadic mapping-cylinder refinement: fibrancy of the constructed middle object

proof.text: By the Joyal model-structure lemma each inner horn is a trivial cofibration and therefore has the left lifting property against every Joyal fibration. Fix such a fibration $p:E\to B$ and a lifting square from $j:X\to M$ to $p$. Extend its given map $X^{(0)}\to E$ recursively. At stage $t$, the existing map supplies the upper map of a lifting square for each horn indexed by $I_t$, and the fixed map $M\to B$ supplies its lower simplex. The lifting property of $p$ gives a filler for each square. Choose these fillers for the small family $I_t$. The pushout universal property of step 1 gives the extension $X^{(t+1)}\to E$; the extensions agree on all earlier stages. The colimit supplies a diagonal $M\to E$ in the original square. Thus $j$ has the left lifting property against every Joyal fibration. By the weak factorization system (trivial cofibrations, fibrations) in that same node, $j$ is a trivial cofibration, hence a categorical equivalence. This explicitly checks closure for this cell sequence rather than assuming a categorical equivalence is preserved by arbitrary colimits.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph beginning “For K”, through the retained operadic mapping-cylinder refinement: categorical equivalence of the relative cell inclusion

proof.text: To apply the Joyal-fibration characterization, let $m$ be a vertex of $M$ and $b:k(m)\to y$ an equivalence edge in $Y$. Its inverse edge maps under $r$ to an inverse for the edge $r(b)$, with the inverse equations witnessed by the images of the two triangles. In $\Delta^1$ the edge $0\to1$ has no reverse edge, so $r(b)$ is degenerate at some endpoint $e$. The edge $b$, its inverse and the two inverse triangles are all in $Y_e$: all their vertices have coordinate $e$, and a simplex of $\Delta^1$ with all vertices $e$ is constant. Also $m\in M_e$. Since $k_e:M_e\to Y_e$ is the identity, the same edge, inverse and triangles in $M_e$ give an equivalence edge with source exactly $m$ lying over $b$. Both $M,Y$ are quasicategories, and $k$ is an inner fibration by step 3. Clause (1) of the cited characterization therefore makes $k$ a Joyal fibration.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph beginning “For K”, through the retained operadic mapping-cylinder refinement: lifting equivalences at their prescribed source

proof.text: The original $a$ is a categorical equivalence by hypothesis and $a=kj$, while $j$ is a categorical equivalence by step 5. Two-out-of-three in the Joyal model structure shows that $k$ is a categorical equivalence. Together with step 6 this makes $k$ a trivial Joyal fibration. Steps 1 and 2 give precisely the required countable continuous composite of pushouts of small coproducts of mixed inner horns, the monomorphism $j$, and unchanged endpoint fibres. If either endpoint fibre is empty, there are no horns or simplices in that fibre requiring separate choices; the same construction and arguments apply. No step uses injectivity of $a$. The additional inner-fibration hypothesis on $r$ is compatible with the proof; the construction in fact only needs the stated quasicategory hypothesis on $Y$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NP-c4253ad7e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all seven steps and checked each against the statements of the five cited nodes (def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones, the presheaf-colimit Mathlib leaf combinedIsColimit, def-coef-infinity-fibrations, lem-coef-joyal-model-structure, and clause (1) of lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations). Checks: (1) I_t is small and the pushouts and colimit are degreewise by the leaf. (2) A nonconstant monotone α has α(0)=0 and α(n)=1, so a constant-coordinate simplex misses 0 or n, and since i≠0,n it lies in Λ^n_i. So no endpoint simplex is added and M_e=X_e literally. (3) The finite-stage gluing of horn faces is correct, and the constant case is filled by v because k_e is the identity. (4) M is a quasicategory, without fibrancy of X. (5) j has the left lifting property against Joyal fibrations by stagewise lifts, so it is a trivial cofibration by the weak factorization system stated in the Joyal node. (6) An equivalence edge in Y has degenerate image in Δ¹, because the witness 2-simplex vertices x,y,x force r(x)=r(y), so its lift lies in M_e=Y_e with the prescribed source; clause (1) then makes k a Joyal fibration. (7) Two-out-of-three on a=kj. The statement is unchanged; the extra hypothesis that r is an inner fibration is unused but harmless. I tested a=id on Δ¹, X=Λ²₁→Δ², non-injective a and empty endpoint fibres. The item is a strictly smaller lemma than parent step 3 of lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-mapping-cylinder, not a restatement of it. lean.note: MixedInnerHorn and mixedInnerHornCell encode the allowed slice cells of this same refinement. RelativeCellComplex of shape ℕ retains the countable continuous cell construction.
